headline: Engineering Student Builds Drones to Deliver Medicine to Flood-Cut Communities
meta_description: Mozambican engineering student Cleiton Michaque has built 14 drones and is testing autonomous delivery to remote communities isolated by floods and poor roads.
summary_short: A Mozambican engineering student has constructed 14 drones from scratch and is now testing an autonomous drone to deliver medicine to communities cut off by flooding.
body:
Mozambican engineering student Cleiton Michaque has built 14 drones from scratch and is currently testing an autonomous drone designed to deliver medicines to remote communities cut off by floods, rivers, and poor roads.

Michaque's initiative addresses a critical gap in healthcare access across Mozambique's most isolated regions. Communities separated by natural barriers and inadequate infrastructure have long struggled to receive timely medical supplies. By designing and building his own drones, Michaque is creating a practical solution grounded in local innovation rather than relying on external resources.

The autonomous delivery system represents a convergence of engineering skill and humanitarian need. Testing the technology in real conditions will determine whether drone delivery can bridge the gap between remote populations and essential medicines, potentially transforming how underserved communities access healthcare.
quick_facts: 14 drones built from scratch by one student
Target: remote communities isolated by floods and poor roads
